entries.unrelatedNote: Four occurrences across four distinct candidate SHAs, none touching packages/experimental/inspector or its dependencies. Two of the four (03a7321e23 and 6decdacb89) are First-100 process-only commits (BLOCKED-QUEUE.md/decisions-approved.md/goal.md/EXEC-STATE.json edits) touching zero product code at all -- the strongest possible unrelatedness evidence, since no source change of any kind was present when the failure occurred. The other two (c60c0f3a4f, af01a06bc96) touch only tests/release/baseline-fingerprint.spec.ts and scripts/release/baseline-fingerprint.mjs (P0-01 slice work), an unrelated package with no dependency relationship to packages/experimental/inspector. Every occurrence reruns clean with zero code changes (confirmed for af01a06bc96 via a same-SHA CI rerun, run 33473101218's second attempt, success). Failure mode each time: a single real-Worker isolated-realm-session test, consistent with a timing-sensitive worker-thread integration test, matching this repo's own history of similar fixes elsewhere (e.g. 'bind fixture servers to OS-assigned ports').
entries.backfillNote:
Rebuilt from CI ARTIFACTS on 2026-09-05, replacing a count maintained by remembering to append. It read 8; the artifact scan puts it at 26.

TWO SEPARATE UNDERCOUNTS, and the second is the instructive one. The first was ordinary lag: occurrences absorbed into green cells were never appended, because greening a cell requires the absorption and nothing requires the record. The second was a BLIND SEARCH: the first attempt to backfill searched the runs' failed-step LOG TEXT for the case name, and returned zero for every run predating cc2511aadb -- the commit that added --reporter=default. Before it, --reporter=json was the only reporter and no human-readable case name reached the log at all (BLOCKED-078). The search was blind for exactly the period before the fix that made logs readable, and it reported that blindness as 'did not fail'. Four runs were rejected as unrelated on that basis; all four in fact failed on this case, which their artifacts state plainly.

THE RULE: a retrospective search is bounded by when its evidence began being recorded, and outside that bound it returns 'nothing found', which is indistinguishable from 'nothing happened'. Correcting it required changing evidence source -- from logs to artifacts -- not searching harder.

Both errors ran in the same direction. Nobody ever forgets to REMOVE an occurrence, and no blind search invents one. That is why this figure is measured rather than accumulated: BLOCKED-080's criterion reads it to decide whether the flake rate is high enough that a failure here stops being distinguishable from a real regression, and every force acting on a remembered count pushes it toward 'safer than it is'.

measuredRate.method: Downloaded the vitest-report.json artifact for all 83 failed runs of first100-exact-sha.yml in the most recent 200-run window (2026-09-01T19:59:01Z to 2026-09-05T07:26:49Z) and matched this case's full name against status=='failed'. 80 of the 83 still had a retrievable artifact; 3 did not.
measuredRate.note: 4 recorded occurrences predate the scan window and could not be re-verified by this method; they are retained. The true lifetime count is therefore at least this figure, not exactly it.

entries.unrelatedNote: BLOCKED-023 same-SHA divergence evidence (2026-09-02): attempt 1 and attempt 2 of CI run 33578193549 ran the byte-identical candidate commit e4390a90a29e71dea1c2d32f3943b4692b5fd933 -- attempt 1 failed this test, attempt 2 passed it, with zero code changes between attempts (a same-SHA rerun). This is the definition of non-determinism: a deterministic failure cannot flip to passing on a byte-identical retry. This test spawns a real CLI subprocess (pnpm run architecture:seams against a real on-disk fixture) as its own acceptance[3] proof, consistent with subprocess-spawning tests being this repository's highest-flake-risk class (matching the already-registered Inspector real-Worker entry's own failure mode). Independently verified: the Supervisor downloaded and byte-compared both attempts' vitest-report.json artifacts (ids 9827604568 and 9828038921) directly from GitHub before registering.
